overview.headline: How gene copies and chromosome location shape inheritance patterns

keyPoints.point: Students learn that autosomal dominant conditions need only one altered copy in each cell to affect a person.
keyPoints.quote: One altered copy of the gene in each cell is sufficient for a person to be affected by an autosomal dominant disorder.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that autosomal recessive inheritance requires variants in both copies of the gene and typically shows unaffected carrier parents.
keyPoints.quote: In autosomal recessive inheritance, variants occur in both copies of the gene in each cell.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that mitochondrial variants are passed only by females because egg cells contribute mitochondria to the developing embryo.
keyPoints.quote: Because only egg cells contribute mitochondria to the developing embryo, only females can pass on mitochondrial variants to their children.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that X-linked inheritance shows no male-to-male transmission because fathers cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons.
keyPoints.quote: A characteristic of X-linked inheritance is that fathers cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons (no male-to-male transmission).

keyTerms.gloss: inheritance where one altered copy in each cell is sufficient to cause disorder
keyTerms.quote: One altered copy of the gene in each cell is sufficient for a person to be affected by an autosomal dominant disorder.

keyTerms.gloss: inheritance where variants occur in both copies of the gene without symptoms in carriers
keyTerms.quote: In autosomal recessive inheritance, variants occur in both copies of the gene in each cell.

keyTerms.gloss: pattern where variants in genes on the X chromosome affect males more frequently than females
keyTerms.quote: X-linked recessive disorders are also caused by variants in genes on the X chromosome.

keyTerms.gloss: maternal pattern where genes in mitochondrial DNA pass only through egg cells to children
keyTerms.quote: Mitochondrial inheritance, also known as maternal inheritance, applies to genes in mitochondrial DNA.

keyTerms.gloss: pattern where an altered gene on the Y chromosome passes only from father to son
keyTerms.quote: A condition is considered Y-linked if the altered gene that causes the disorder is located on the Y chromosome

keyTerms.gloss: inheritance where two alleles are both expressed and make slightly different proteins
keyTerms.quote: In codominant inheritance, two different versions (alleles) of a gene are expressed, and each version makes a slightly different protein.
